newsitem.title: USA: Pilots say "not that far apart" in talks.
newsitem.headline: Pilots say "not that far apart" in talks.

text.p: An American Airlines pilots union spokesman said Thursday "we're not that far apart" on terms for a new contract which would avert a strike scheduled for midnight Friday.
Allied Pilots Association spokesman Wally Pitts said it was possible to reach an agreement and head off the threatened strike. "We're not that far apart," he told reporters.
The most contentious issues between the union and American are pay and which pilots would fly the new smaller jets the carrier intends to buy for its regional airline, American Eagle.

American wants to have lower-paid Eagle pilots from another union fly them, while the Allied Pilots Association wants its members to fly the aircraft. American has said it needed the lower-paid pilots in order to be competitive with other major carriers which have low-cost regional airline services.
The union late last night made an offer to accept lower pay for its members who would fly the smaller jets, provided the jets flew under the "American Airlines" banner and not that of Eagle.
Discussing pay, Pitts said there were only a couple of percentage points between the American offer and the union demand and that American "can afford" to reconcile the pay differences.
